subject: Riverfront production throughput regression — urgent runbook & exec sync
messages:
From: Tom Lang <tom.lang@riverfront.ai>
To: Riverfront Support <support@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Riverfront SRE <sre@riverfront.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse + 500s since 03:00 PDT

Hey team,

We woke up to a sharp drop in throughput for our production integration at ~03:00 PDT — throughput is down ~65% vs baseline and p99 latency is spiking into seconds; we're also seeing an elevated 5xx rate (mostly 503s and some 500s). This started after your scheduled kernel/optimizer rollout; no config change on our side.

I've attached a short trace and service logs (svc-logs-20270429.tar.gz) and a heatmap that shows hot prefixes. The SRE team notes rapid KV eviction churn on the model-serving layer and repeated HOL stalls. Can you confirm whether the rollout changed batching or KV allocation behavior? We are in active incident mode and this is customer-facing for our LLM feature.

Please advise immediate mitigation and ETA for a fix — we may need a rollback or a capacity isolation until this is stable.

- Tom
Lead SRE, Riverfront.ai

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Tom Lang <tom.lang@riverfront.ai>
Cc: Riverfront SRE <sre@riverfront.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse + 500s since 03:00 PDT

Tom — thanks for the quick data. We're looking into it now. Initial triage from ops indicates the new batching kernel that shipped last night has an aggressive coalescing heuristic that can cause larger combined batches for some traffic shapes. When combined with the current KV cache TTL and prefix allocation we can get tight eviction/reload cycles that induce head-of-line stalls for hot prefixes.

Immediate actions we're taking:
- Enable fallback routing to the previous kernel for Riverfront (rolling now, expected 10 min).
- Temporarily increase per-tenant KV reservation for Riverfront by 2x to avoid eviction churn.
- Pin top-10 hot prefixes for 30 minutes (prevent eviction while we observe).

I'll update in 15 mins with telemetry after the rollback/fallback completes. Attaching the eviction sample Tom shared for the team.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden throughput collapse + 500s — need exec sync and credit plan

Thanks, Van. Rapid notes from triage (ops + runtime):

Summary of likely mechanism (needs RCA):
- The new batching/coalescing kernel increases batch size heuristically when it sees many short, similar requests within a small time window. That is normally good for throughput.
- For Riverfront's traffic pattern we observed frequent short prefix spikes (many different short prefixes that nonetheless map to a small set of "hot" keys). Because their KV TTL was relatively short (45s) and tenancy reservation modest, these larger batches led to cache churn: hot prefixes were being evicted then reloaded repeatedly.
- Eviction + reload creates tiny sequential stalls on the hotshard path: when a request misses, we block-prefetch which temporarily blocks the lane (HOL). The batching kernel exacerbates this by creating larger batches that wait on the same hotkey prefetch. Net effect: higher p99 latency and higher 5xx as backpressure propagates.

Immediate mitigations done / in-flight:
- Fallback routing to previous kernel complete for Riverfront (rolled in 9 minutes).
- Increase tenant KV reservation = deployed (2x).
- Pin top prefixes = deployed. Preliminary telemetry shows error rate dropping and throughput recovering (see attached hotlane-graphs.png).

Short-term actionable plan (24h):
1) Keep fallback kernel for Riverfront until we validate a kernel fix.
2) Ship a conservative coalescing threshold in the batching kernel (reduce batch_max_latency and batch_growth_factor) so it doesn't combine requests across hot prefix churn. Target patch in 6-12 hours; quick canary on small fleet.
3) Add adaptive prefix-pin logic (auto-detect eviction-churn) as a guardrail within 48 hours.
4) Post-mortem within 72 hours with detailed KV metrics and timeline.

Jonas/Ben — can you confirm the exec brief cadence? Ben, the customer will ask about credits and escalation SLA. I'll provide the technical slides for the brief.

-Grace
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Tom / Riverfront SRE — thank you for the data and patience. Quick update: we've routed Riverfront traffic to the previous stable kernel (fallback) and increased their KV reservation; initial telemetry indicates throughput has recovered to ~92% of baseline and p99 latency has dropped significantly. We're scheduling a 30-minute exec & technical sync at 17:00 PDT today to walk through mitigations and next steps (invite sent).

Ben will follow up on a temporary service credit and our post-mortem timeline. We take this seriously and will deliver a full RCA within 72 hours.

Vanessa — please keep the pinned prefixes and the fallback until we've validated the conservative coalescing patch. Grace — prioritize the canary patch; ops will assist with rollout gating and monitoring.

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
